frontier.hypothesis: The whole remaining residual is one cluster - the cse_set_around_loop hoist of the D_800A3558 and D_800A35B0 reads out of the second loop body into its guard block and its tail - and the do/while chassis is now 17 points closer to the target than it was when s7-s10 framed that question, so the frontier is unchanged but far cheaper to close.
frontier.mechanism: cse.c:7909 cse_set_around_loop only acts on values flagged REG_LOOP_TEST_P (cse.c:7936), and the only setter of that flag is jump.c's duplicate_loop_exit_test, which requires a top-test loop. s10 proved the top-test chassis pays 24 frame bytes (three combine-orphaned '(use (reg))' pseudos typed ST_REGS) for that hoist. The question s11 did NOT get to is whether the four new statement-level levers apply to the top-test chassis too: it was 49 with the OLD body, and if L2-L4 are worth anything like 17 points there as well, its 24-byte frame penalty (about 13 insns) may now be affordable.
frontier.next_probe: Port levers L2, L3 and L4 (the geom/static temp pair at both pre-loop sites and in the body, and prim.link before prim.code at both call sites - NOT L1, which s7 measured backwards on that chassis) onto memory/grind/func_80070C70/chassis-toptest-shapeexact-49.c and score it with tmp/grind/func_80070C70/s11/score.sh. If it lands below 22 the chassis question reopens with a real number instead of a strategic argument. If it does not, read tools/gcc-2.7.2/cse.c's cse_around_loop / invalidate_skipped_block path with the .cse and .cse2 dumps of the 22-point body open (tmp/grind/func_80070C70/s10/scan.py extracts the func section) and enumerate the SOURCE-side inputs to that predicate.

frontier.hypothesis: The three 'addiu $v1,$v0,K' sites are now matched but two smaller ordering diffs remain that were never isolated: the position of 'sw $s3,0x2C($sp)' in the first loop, and the nop the target keeps after 'lw $v0,0x18($s1)' in the second loop's guard where our build fills the slot.
frontier.mechanism: Both are sched1/reorg outcomes downstream of what else is ready in the same cycle. The first-loop one moved once already this session (it disappeared between q3 and r1 when prim.link was read before prim.code), which is evidence that call-argument statement order is the knob for that block rather than the store order itself.
frontier.next_probe: Re-diff the 22-point body (tmp/grind/func_80070C70/s9/dis.sh after installing candidate.c) and enumerate statement orders for the FIRST loop's four body statements (prim.mode, prim.link, prim.code, the call) the way s11 did for the second loop - only two of the six orders have been measured.

frontier.hypothesis: IconC70's trailing 24 bytes still have a placeholder member list ('s16 sp50[12]'), and recovering the real one remains a prerequisite for any submission. Carried unspent from s1/s2/s3 and now the single largest correctness risk on a body that is 22 points from matching.
frontier.mechanism: Correctness of the submitted C, not codegen. The 0x20 SIZE is proven three ways (frame arithmetic in s1, the BB2_FRAME_DEBUG census in s6, s10's 'stack_temp mode=26 size=32'), but the field list is not evidence-backed and the Judge will read it.
frontier.next_probe: Read the $a1-relative stores in func_80069898's other callers - func_8006B120, func_8006CFBC, func_800720FC, func_80074488, func_8006F97C - and build the true field list, then propagate the corrected type to func_8006F97C's ledger, an active queue sibling in the same TU.
